subject: Processor coverage + data residency matrix request for upcoming audit
messages:
From: Audrey Lin <audrey.lin@medihelp.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medihelp.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency and subprocessor coverage — upcoming compliance review

Hi Stephanie,

Hope you’re well. We have a scheduled vendor compliance audit next month and our security team requested a consolidated matrix that shows:

- Which subprocessors Redwood uses for telemetry, logging, observability, and backups
- Where (country/region) data is at rest for each subprocessor and any cross-border transfers
- Any temporary third-party access (e.g., contractor consoles, engineering VPN) and the justification window

Can you provide a single CSV/slide that captures the above and indicate whether any of the processors handle PHI (we are a healthcare customer)? If you have an existing template we’ll accept that.

We need this by COB Friday 7/6 to feed into our internal evidence pack. Appreciate a short note if there are blockers.

Thanks,
Audrey Lin
Vendor Risk Manager
MediHelp Health Systems

--
Attachment: (none)
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Audrey Lin <audrey.lin@medihelp.com>, procurement@medihelp.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency and subprocessor coverage — upcoming compliance review

Hi Kim / Grace,

Audrey from MediHelp just requested a consolidated processor/residency matrix and PHI handling flags for their audit. They need it by 7/6 COB. I’ve copied the ask below.

Can you each own the following and I’ll stitch into a single CSV?

- Kimberly: Observability, logs, metrics, and any third-party tracing (list services, countries, whether logs contain request headers/body samples).
- Grace: Backup/storage, object store providers, key management (KMS/HSM), and any cross-border replication.

Key constraints: minimize manual escalations — call out if a processor is transient (contractor access) versus persistent (vendor-managed storage). For PHI, mark yes/no and add a short note on whether we have a DPA clause that restricts processing or requires additional safeguards.

I’ll handle the cover note and run legal/ctrls sign-off if either of you flag anything sensitive. If it helps, I’ve started a draft CSV and uploaded to the team drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleSharedLink

Thanks — can you confirm ownership and estimated ETA (EOD Wed/7/3 ideally)?

-Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Security & Compliance (Customer Programs)
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Audrey Lin <audrey.lin@medihelp.com>, procurement@medihelp.com
Date: Wed, 03 Jul 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency and subprocessor coverage — upcoming compliance review

Stephanie — confirmed, I’ll take observability and logging. Preliminary notes below (I’m attaching a CSV extract):

- LogIngest (internal product name) / vendor: LogStreamCo — primary region us-west-2; backups replicated to eu-west-1 for disaster recovery. Logs: sampling at 0.1%, request headers only by default; body capture off (rarely enabled by request). PHI handling: NO by default; noted exceptions when customers opt-in for full request capture (we document and DPA addendum required).

- Traces / vendor: Tracenow — hosted in us-east-1; data retention defaults 30 days. PHI handling: NO.

- Metrics / vendor: MetricsPlus — global; no PII/PHI collected.

Temporary access: engineering support contractors sometimes granted 7-day console access via SSO/JIT. We keep access logs and require justification notes in the access ticket.

I attached processor_matrix_v1.csv (extract) and added fields for PHI_flag, retention_days, cross_border (yes/no), and control_refs.

ETA: I’ll finish population and send final CSV by EOD 7/4.

-Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Observability Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: processor_matrix_v1.csv
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Audrey Lin <audrey.lin@medihelp.com>, procurement@medihelp.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2028 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Processor coverage and residency matrix — MediHelp evidence pack (attached)

Audrey / Procurement team,

Thanks for the patience — please find attached the consolidated processor/residency matrix and temporary access instructions. High level:

- Processors listed with vendor name, region(s) of primary processing, cross-border flag, PHI handling indicator, retention window, and control references (SOC2/SLA/DPA clauses).
- PHI handling: None of the default telemetry vendors ingest PHI for MediHelp by default. Where customers enable full request capture, we require an addendum and explicit authorisation; those vendors are flagged.
- Temporary access: we included the operational pattern for short-lived contractor access and attached VPN/JIT instructions (temporary_vpn_instructions.pdf).

Attachments: processor_matrix_v1.csv, temporary_vpn_instructions.pdf

Next steps: If your security team wants a short walkthrough of the matrix, we can schedule a 30-minute session early next week. Otherwise, please let us know if anything requires redaction or further evidence (e.g., SOC2 control IDs).

Best,
-Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Security & Compliance (Customer Programs)
Redwood Inference
